episode.title: Safely adapt SDK endpoint options to the selected provider interface
episode.before: At parent c5ad0abb5de461416306a516ddbb26dc78f87d40, the content-generator configuration could carry an explicit baseUrl, and client creation forwarded that value directly to GoogleGenAI. It did not read the provider-specific GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL environment variables, did not validate custom endpoint URLs, and passed config.vertexai through unchanged, leaving it undefined when the authentication type identified a provider but credential inference had not populated the flag.
episode.after: At cb289e0724b46ce867b6d3fe4bd0ac6ed890dc45, GoogleGenAI client creation first prefers an explicit baseUrl, otherwise selects the environment endpoint associated with the authentication type, validates any selected custom endpoint as a URL and requires HTTPS except for localhost loopback hosts, forwards the accepted endpoint through httpOptions.baseUrl, and derives the SDK vertexai mode from the Vertex authentication type when the explicit flag is absent. Tests cover both provider branches, explicit-over-environment precedence, provider selection without inferred credentials, localhost HTTP, malformed URLs, and insecure remote HTTP.
episode.diff: The implementation added a custom-endpoint validator and provider-aware endpoint resolution inside the GoogleGenAI construction branch. It replaced direct config.baseUrl forwarding with explicit-first, authentication-directed resolution from two environment variables; rejected malformed or insecure remote endpoints; and changed the SDK mode argument from config.vertexai to config.vertexai ?? (authType is the Vertex branch). The test suite added seven focused cases and updated existing SDK-constructor expectations to require a concrete false mode for the non-Vertex branch. Documentation added the two environment contracts and their transport restrictions.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-provider-endpoint-precedence
candidate_atomics.title: Resolve a provider-specific endpoint with explicit configuration precedence
candidate_atomics.description: Select the endpoint candidate at the provider-client boundary: retain an explicit runtime endpoint when present; otherwise read the environment slot associated with the declared authentication interface.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure custom requests target the endpoint belonging to the selected provider interface without allowing an environment default to override an explicit caller choice.
semantic_action.pre_state: Client configuration may contain an explicit endpoint, either provider-specific environment endpoint may be present, and the declared authentication type identifies the active interface.
semantic_action.post_state: At most one endpoint candidate is selected; explicit configuration wins, and an environment fallback is chosen according to the declared authentication type rather than inferred credentials.
semantic_action.validation: Mock the external SDK constructor and assert both provider environment branches, both-environment disambiguation under an explicit authentication type, and explicit-over-environment precedence.

candidate_atomics.name: guard-custom-endpoint-transport
candidate_atomics.title: Reject malformed or insecure remote custom endpoints
candidate_atomics.description: Parse any selected custom endpoint and enforce encrypted transport for remote hosts while retaining an HTTP exception for local loopback development.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent invalid or insecure remote endpoint overrides from reaching the provider SDK while preserving local development connectivity.
semantic_action.pre_state: A non-empty explicit or environment-derived custom endpoint has been selected but has not yet been admitted to outbound client options.
semantic_action.post_state: The endpoint is admitted only if it is parseable and uses HTTPS, except that named and numeric loopback hosts may use HTTP; rejected values fail before SDK construction.
semantic_action.validation: Assert acceptance of an HTTP loopback URL and rejection of both an unparsable string and an HTTP remote URL with the expected error classes/messages.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-provider-sdk-options
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile provider identity and forward accepted options to the SDK
candidate_atomics.description: Construct the provider SDK options with the validated endpoint and a concrete provider-mode flag, deriving the mode from the declared authentication interface when upstream credential inference left it unset.

semantic_action.intent: Keep endpoint routing and SDK provider mode consistent at the external-provider interface even when optional configuration fields were not populated upstream.
semantic_action.pre_state: Endpoint resolution and admission have completed, while the SDK provider-mode field may be explicitly set or absent despite a declared authentication type.
semantic_action.post_state: The SDK receives the accepted endpoint in its HTTP options and a concrete provider-mode value that preserves an explicit setting or otherwise reflects the declared authentication interface.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the mocked SDK constructor for endpoint forwarding and correct true/false provider-mode values, including the branch with declared cloud authentication but no inferred credentials and established non-cloud scenarios.

candidate_workflows.name: safely-adapt-provider-endpoint-configuration
candidate_workflows.title: Safely route custom endpoints through a multi-provider SDK boundary
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for honoring explicit and environment-supplied endpoint overrides while preserving provider identity, transport safety, and existing client behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: Construct the external provider client with the intended custom endpoint and matching provider mode, while rejecting malformed or insecure remote overrides before any request can use them.
when_to_use: A client supports multiple provider interfaces selected by an authentication or backend mode.
Callers need endpoint overrides through both an explicit configuration field and provider-specific environment variables.
The external SDK accepts endpoint and provider-mode options that must remain mutually consistent.
anti_goals: Do not change authentication credential precedence or introduce new credential requirements.
Do not apply these endpoint environment variables to unrelated authentication paths or alternate client implementations.
Do not permit remote plaintext HTTP merely to maximize compatibility.
Do not let an environment endpoint override a caller-supplied explicit endpoint.
not_applicable_when: The integration has only one provider interface and no competing endpoint sources.
Endpoint selection and validation are already owned and guaranteed by a lower-level SDK contract.
The target path does not construct the SDK client that consumes the custom endpoint.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The client-construction boundary knows the declared authentication type, but provider-specific endpoint environment variables are ignored, custom endpoints are not transport-validated, and SDK provider mode may be absent.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The SDK receives the highest-precedence endpoint associated with the declared provider and a consistent concrete provider mode; malformed and insecure remote endpoints fail before client construction.

steps.condition: Run when constructing a provider SDK client for a supported direct-provider authentication branch.
steps.validation: Constructor-focused tests demonstrate provider-directed environment lookup, explicit precedence, and selection based on declared authentication type even without inferred credentials.

steps.condition: Run only when endpoint resolution yields a non-empty custom endpoint.
steps.validation: Unit tests prove loopback HTTP acceptance and rejection of malformed or remote HTTP values.

steps.condition: Run after an endpoint is admitted, or directly with no endpoint when resolution yields none; preserve an explicit provider-mode value when supplied.
steps.validation: Mocked constructor assertions prove accepted endpoint forwarding and concrete provider-mode reconciliation for both provider branches and existing non-cloud cases.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: confirm endpoint lookup is inside the intended SDK-construction branch and keyed by the declared authentication type.
Focused unit checks: verify each provider environment endpoint is forwarded with the matching provider mode.
Precedence check: set explicit and environment endpoints and verify the explicit value wins.
Safety checks: verify loopback HTTP succeeds while malformed and remote HTTP endpoints fail before SDK construction.
Regression checks: retain established constructor-option assertions, now with concrete non-cloud provider mode.
Repository test execution: run the focused content-generator test file in an intact checkout; this remained deferred in the supplied staged-deletion worktree.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the declared provider cannot be determined at the client-construction boundary.
Stop if no direct test seam can observe the external SDK constructor options or rejection behavior.
Stop rather than broadening scope if endpoint support would require changing credential acquisition or unrelated authentication paths.
Do not claim runtime validation success until the focused tests execute in an intact checkout.
